actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides and new growth with a flashlight for thrips
Check whether spots are raised corky bumps (edema) or flat lesions
Check top 2–3 cm of soil with finger every few days
Water thoroughly at the soil when dry and let it drain fully
Ensure pot has a drainage hole and empty standing water from the cachepot
Repot into a chunky aroid mix (potting soil, bark, perlite)
Move plant to bright indirect light with airflow, away from the wall
Remove heavily spotted leaves with clean scissors
Monitor for new spots over 2–3 weeks
If new spots keep appearing, apply copper-based fungicide per label

reason: The answer correctly names fungal leaf spot as the main issue, but the copper fungicide that fixed it is only a conditional last step after weeks of watering changes, and nothing it recommends is likely to harm the plant.
